core_obligations: Identify the category of quasi-coherent modules on the big site with the quasi-coherent modules on S via the pullback G of a quasi-coherent module on S, and record which constructions that identification commutes with (proof lines 3542-3545).
For direct sums: write each quasi-coherent F_i on the big site as G_i^a and commute the direct sum with the pullback (proof lines 3548-3552).
For arbitrary colimits: carry a diagram on the index category to a diagram G_i on S and commute the colimit with the pullback (proof lines 3555-3560).
For cokernels: write a morphism on the big site as b^a for a morphism b on S and use that a cokernel is a colimit (proof lines 3563-3568).
For the middle term of a short exact sequence: use part (10) of the equivalence lemma on the two outer terms (proof lines 3571-3575).
For tensor products: commute the tensor product of the pullbacks with the pullback of the tensor product on S (proof lines 3578-3585).

For internal homs: pull back to a quasi-coherent H on S, observe H is finite locally free, reduce by a Zariski local argument on S to H free of finite rank, and read off that the internal hom is a finite direct sum of copies of the second argument (proof lines 3588-3596).
proof_roadmap: Set up the transfer through the equivalence of quasi-coherent modules on the big site with those on S (proof lines 3542-3545).
Middle term of a short exact sequence (proof lines 3571-3575).
Internal hom into a quasi-coherent module out of a finite locally free one, by Zariski local reduction to a finite free module (proof lines 3588-3596).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme S and a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf, the lemma lists six closure properties of the category of quasi-coherent modules on the big site of S: direct sums, arbitrary colimits, cokernels, the middle term of a short exact sequence whose outer terms are quasi-coherent, tensor products, and internal homs with a finite locally free first argument (statement lines 3514-3539). The proof is one uniform transfer: the equivalence of quasi-coherent modules on the big site with quasi-coherent modules on S, given by pullback along the structure maps, commutes with each of the six constructions in turn, and each of the six facts then holds because the corresponding fact holds for quasi-coherent modules on the scheme S (proof lines 3542-3545). Five of the six parts are one line each precisely because that commutation is all that is needed (proof lines 3548-3560, 3563-3568, 3571-3575, 3578-3585), while part (6) adds a Zariski local reduction that the author marks as omitted details (proof lines 3588-3596). The claim is H2: the substance is the identification of each of the six constructions as the construction on S followed by the big-site pullback, and no part requires more than that, so this is a complete but routine derivation and not one of the multi-argument or extra-criterion cases.
